title: Architecture & Standards: API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance, and ADRs
author: Michael Chen
body:
Purpose
-------
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's cross-cutting architecture and standards for API design, coding practices, infrastructure, model-serving, observability, performance goals, and the Decision Record (ADR) process. Intended audience: engineering teams (platform, runtime, infra), product, and SRE. It is a canonical reference for how new services and features should be designed and evaluated for production readiness.

Summary of scope
----------------
- API standards: request/response conventions, versioning, error model, authentication, rate limits.
- Coding standards: repo layout, linting, testing, dependency management.
- Infra standards: IaC, networking, capacity, secrets, tenancy models.
- Model-serving standards: model versioning, quantization profiles, rollout policies, hardware mapping.
- Observability: required metrics, traces, logs, dashboards, and alerting thresholds.
- Performance standards: SLOs, benchmarking methodology, latency/cost budgets.
- ADRs: how we document major architectural choices and their rationale.

1) API Standards
----------------
Intro: APIs are Redwood's primary contract with customers and downstream services. We prioritize stability, discoverability, and clear failure semantics.
Must-have rules:
- Use RESTful JSON over HTTPS for public-facing endpoints; internal RPC (gRPC) allowed for high-throughput internal calls.
- Endpoint naming: kebab-case, resource-oriented. Example: POST /v1/models/{model-id}/infer.
- Versioning: path-based versioning (e.g., /v1/) for breaking changes. Non-breaking additions must remain backward compatible.
- Schema: responses must include a top-level "meta" object with keys: request_id, server_time_ms, model_version. Example response skeleton in JSON:

{
  "meta": { "request_id": "<uuid>", "server_time_ms": 42, "model_version": "rwood-1.3.0" },
  "data": { "outputs": [ ... ] }
}

- Error model: return standard HTTP codes plus structured error payload: { "error": { "code": "string_code", "message": "human-friendly", "details": optional } }. Document common error codes per API (e.g., RATE_LIMIT, MODEL_NOT_AVAILABLE, INVALID_INPUT).
- Authentication: OAuth2 for customer-facing APIs + API keys for service accounts. Short-lived tokens for internal services, rotated via KMS.
- Pagination: use cursor-based pagination for large collections.
- Rate limiting: default per-tenant rate limits (tokens/sec) and global per-route throttles. Rate-limit responses must include Retry-After header and a structured error code RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED.
- Contract testing: every public API must have a contract test suite (example: Pact or OpenAPI-based tests) run in CI and gating for merging changes.

2) Coding Standards
-------------------
Principles: readability, small functions, observable behavior, and testability.
Language-specific rules (brief):
- Python: use Black, isort, flake8; prefer dataclasses over mutable dicts for structured types.
- Go: gofmt, go vet, generated docs for public packages.
- TypeScript: strict mode, ESLint + Prettier.

Repo and CI conventions:
1. One service per repo is preferred unless tightly coupled libraries share a mono-repo.
2. CI must run linting, unit tests, contract tests, and a lightweight integration smoke test.
3. Every change to infra or runtime that can affect customer traffic must require an explicit approver from the service owner and SRE.

Testing matrix:
- Unit tests: >= 80% for core business logic.
- Integration tests: provide coverage for critical paths (model loading, caching, auth).
- Load tests: staged for any change that touches request path or infra configs.

3) Infrastructure Standards
---------------------------
IaC and provisioning:
- Terraform is the canonical IaC tool. Use modules under terraform/modules and versioned module registry.
- All state files must be stored in encrypted remote state (S3 + DynamoDB locking) per-account.
- Resource naming convention: rwood-{env}-{team}-{service}-{resource}.

Networking and security:
- All production services must run in private subnets; only edge proxies are internet-facing.
- mTLS required for internal RPC calls where feasible; otherwise enforce strict IAM.
- Security groups: deny-by-default, least-privilege egress/ingress.

Secrets and keys:
- Use central KMS (cloud KMS / HSM) for keys, with access audited.
- No secrets in plaintext in repos or logs; scan commits for secrets in CI.

Capacity, scaling, and tenancy:
- Dedicated vs shared capacity: Dedicated pools for enterprise tenants with regulatory needs, shared pools for hosted API traffic.
- Autoscaling policies must guard against cascading failures: use CPU/GPU utilization + queue depth + P99 latency signals.
- Capacity planning doc must be maintained quarterly with target headroom (default 30% spare GPU capacity in each region).

4) Model-serving Standards
--------------------------
Goals: deterministic latency profiles, predictable cost, and model quality guardrails.
Model onboarding checklist (must be completed before a model serves production traffic):
1. Model metadata: architecture, size, tokenizer, training data summary, license, recommended precision/quantization.
2. Performance benchmark: throughput (tokens/s), P50/P90/P99 latency on target hardware, and memory requirements.
3. Quantization profile: validated accuracy loss for INT8/FP16 variants with representative eval set.
4. Safety/quality evals: pass Redwood quality guards and a set of enterprise-specific prompt tests.
5. Rollout playbook: canary traffic %, rollback steps, monitoring dashboards, and slice-based quality checks.

Runtime requirements:
- Model versions are immutable. Use semantic versioning for model packages (e.g., bert-qa-1.2.0).
- KV cache and prefix caching: runtime should expose knobs for cache TTL and max entries; defaults must be documented per model.
- Fallbacks: define compatible fallback families (e.g., if rwood-7b quantized unavailable, route to rwood-7b-fp16 or a higher-latency but validated model) in policy config.

Model routing policy example (YAML):

routing_policy:
  - priority: low-cost
    match: { max_latency_ms: 200 }
    target: rwood-7b-int8
  - priority: fallback
    match: { any: true }
    target: rwood-7b-fp16

5) Observability Standards
--------------------------
Signals required for every service:
- Metrics (Prometheus format): request_count, request_latency_ms{quantiles}, error_count, token_generated_count, model_load_time_ms, cache_hit_rate.
- Traces: every external request must propagate a Trace ID. Spans should include model_version and route metadata.
- Logs: structured JSON logs, include request_id and severity; no PII.
- Dashboards: per-service overview (throughput, latency P50/P90/P99, error rate), per-model quality (eval pass/fail, recent regressions).

Alerting thresholds (typical):
- P99 latency > 800ms for > 5m -> SEV2 alert.
- Error rate > 1% of requests for > 5m -> SEV1 if impacting customer SLAs.
- Model load time > 10s -> Pager to runtime-oncall.

Logging retention and access:
- Standard retention: 30 days for debug logs, 365 days for audit logs (security/privileged operations). Access to audit logs is restricted.

6) Performance Standards and Benchmarking
---------------------------------------
SLOs and budgets (platform default):
- Latency SLOs (hosted API): P50 < 50ms, P90 < 120ms, P99 < 300ms for typical conversational models on optimized hardware.
- Availability SLO: 99.9% monthly for hosted API; dedicated customers may have higher SLAs per contract.
- Cost budget: target cost-per-token based on model class; teams must attach expected cost budgets before rollout.

Benchmarking methodology:
- Use standard harness (eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite) with controlled datasets and synthetic concurrency patterns that reflect production mix.
- Report: throughput (tokens/s), latency distribution, GPU utilization, memory usage, and end-to-end cost estimate. Include environment spec (GPU type, driver, runtime).

Performance regression process:
1. Baseline benchmarking for every merge to main for runtime and model infra.
2. If P50/P90/P99 degrade by > 10% relative to baseline, open a regression triage ticket tagged performance-regression and block release until mitigated or approved by performance owner.

7) ADR Process (Decision Records)
--------------------------------
Purpose: capture significant architectural decisions, alternatives considered, and consequences.
Where to store: confluence/architecture-and-standards/adrs (and mirror a copy in the repo under docs/adrs).
ADR template (standard fields):
- Title
- Status (proposed | accepted | superseded)
- Context and problem statement
- Decision (what we decided)
- Consequences (pros/cons, operational cost)
- Alternatives considered
- Date & Author

Example ADR summary:
- Title: Choose TFServing vs Custom Runtime for quantized models
- Status: accepted
- Decision: use Custom runtime (rwood-runtime) because it supports fused kernels and GPU memory optimizations required for stable P99 latency.
- Consequences: higher maintenance burden but ~25% lower P99 latency on target workloads.

8) Review & Governance
----------------------
- All cross-cutting changes to standards require a review by the Architecture Working Group (AWG). Schedule: biweekly sync; ad-hoc reviews for urgent proposals.
- Any change affecting SLOs, security posture, or infra cost > 10% must include sign-off from SRE, Security, and Finance.

9) Onboarding checklist for teams (short)
---------------------------------------
- Read this standards doc and confirm owner and reviewers.
- Fill out the Service Readiness Form (link: /confluence/eng-platform/service-readiness-form).
- Provide benchmarks and model onboarding checklist items in a PR.
- Create dashboards and alert rules as per observability standards.

--------------------------------

Appendix A: Minimal required metadata for new services
----------------------------------------------------
| Field | Description | Owner |
|-------|-------------|-------|
| service_name | short kebab-case name | service_owner |
| contact | paged rotation | service_owner |
| expected_qps | planned peak QPS | product |
| target_slo | e.g. P99 < 300ms | service_owner |
| monitoring_dash | link to dashboard | observability_owner |

--------------------------------
